idiom_name: factory returning an object over a Map with a journal array
implementation_notes: The fake is an ordinary object (or small class) closing over a Map for state and an array for the journal; nothing of the classic structure has to be built, and the accessor is a plain method. Jest's mock functions cover the recording half - fn.mock.calls, mock.results, toHaveBeenCalledWith - but only with mockImplementation do they also behave, and even then the journal holds raw arguments rather than domain operations, so the library belongs to the spy row and the hand-written journal is preferred when assertions should read as operations. Export a factory rather than a module-level singleton so every test gets fresh state, and let Jest's clearMocks option handle library-side records between tests.
pitfalls: A module-level store or journal is shared by every test that imports it - export a factory and build the fake per test.
Pushing live objects into the journal lets later mutation rewrite the recorded history; record copies, or freeze the entries.
An object literal silently loses methods when the collaborator interface grows; type the fake against the collaborator in TypeScript or keep a contract test.
